fixes.explanation: Yes, baker. Paul writes, "I took Titus along also." (Galatians 2:1) So he went up to Jerusalem with Barnabas and Titus both. Titus comes up again in verse 3.
Silas is a good guess, friend. Acts tells us Paul chose Silas and left (Acts 15:40). But on this Jerusalem trip, Paul names Titus: "I took Titus along also." (Galatians 2:1)

Timothy was a disciple Paul wanted to take along on a trip (Acts 16:1-3). That's a fine name to land on, since Paul had plenty of partners. But for this trip, Paul says, "I took Titus along also." (Galatians 2:1) I mix up my cookie cutter kids' names sometimes too, and I only have six.

That's it. Paul says, "But I spoke privately to those recognized as leaders…" (Galatians 2:2) He sets before them the gospel he preaches among the Gentiles, and he speaks privately to the recognized leaders. I'd say it's like pulling the head baker aside for a quiet word about the batch.
The scribes and Pharisees are a fair guess, friend. But Paul never mentions them in this passage. He says he spoke privately to "…those recognized as leaders…" (Galatians 2:2)

Paul doesn't say anything about priests or the temple in these verses. The people he names are "…those recognized as leaders…" (Galatians 2:2) Jerusalem is a big place, friend, so it's easy to picture a different crowd.
Good thinking to weigh it, baker. But Paul says the opposite: "…not even Titus, who was with me, was compelled to be circumcised, even though he was a Greek." (Galatians 2:3) So the answer is False.
Right, baker. Paul says, "…not even Titus, who was with me, was compelled to be circumcised, even though he was a Greek." (Galatians 2:3) The word is "compelled." Nobody forced it on Titus.
You got it, baker. Paul says they came "…to spy on our freedom in Christ Jesus…" (Galatians 2:4) They didn't come as honest visitors. They came in under false pretenses.

That's the reason, baker. Paul writes, "…whatever they were makes no difference to me; God does not show favoritism…" (Galatians 2:6) Their reputation isn't what Paul points to. The reason he gives is that God does not show favoritism.
You got it, baker. Paul says, "…those leaders added nothing to me." (Galatians 2:6) Think of showing someone your finished batch and hearing, "Nothing to add here."
Paul says the reverse, baker. His words are, "…those leaders added nothing to me." (Galatians 2:6) So the answer is True. The leaders added nothing to him.

Yes, baker. Paul says they "…gave me and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship…" (Galatians 2:9) They did it recognizing the grace Paul had been given. It's a handshake, friend, and it says they're on the same team.

That's the request, baker. Paul says, "They only asked us to remember the poor…" (Galatians 2:10) A list that short even I could remember, and I'm the stamper who once lost track of a whole batch in the oven. Just one ask, and it's about the poor.

I see why that might sound right, friend. People often have to be nudged toward a request. But Paul says remembering the poor was "…the very thing I was eager to do." (Galatians 2:10) Nobody had to talk him into it.
